- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.2) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price deviates >3σ from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average with decay factor (e.g., 0.85 per day).
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent sentiment; if sentiment is volatile or mixed, use 7-day sentiment average instead of 18-day to reduce noise.
- When sentiment is flat (0.0–0.2) and price is stable, model tends to forecast downward; if true outcome is rising, add 1–2% to forecast to avoid “false bearishness”.
